defs.text: If something is easy, it is comfortable.

defs.text: A check is a piece of paper that gives someone else the right to receive some money from your bank account. (Other spelling: cheque)

defs.text: A check is something you do to make sure that there is no problem.

defs.text: If you check something, you look at it to see if there is a problem, or something new or different.

defs.text: If you check something out, you look at it because it might be interesting.

defs.example: If you want to get mail from us, check the box at the bottom of the page.

defs.text: If you check out of a hotel, you pay your bill and leave.

defs.text: A deal is a situation.

defs.text: A body is the main part of a person, animal, physical object, or organisation.

defs.text: A body is a dead person or animal.

defs.text: A body is a group of people.

defs.example: Lake Michigan is a large body of water.

defs.example: I'm afraid of snakes. I can't even go near them.

defs.text: Sleep is the activity or time of resting quietly with eyes shut, usually in bed for many hours at night.
If you sleep, you rest quietly with eyes shut, usually in bed for many hours at night.
defs.example: I need to sleep now because I'm tired.

defs.text: If you sleep with someone, you have sex with them.

defs.text: Something that can happen.

defs.text: Something that is random; luck.

defs.text: How much something is likely to be true.

defs.text: Dear is something that is precious or greatly valued to someone. They love the thing or the person.
defs.example: My large stamp collection is very dear to me.

defs.text: A kind, loving person.

defs.text: The number 4.

defs.text: You use anyway to say something does not matter, or you do not care.

defs.example: Jesse and Anne had a big fight. That's what I heard anyway.

defs.example: Yeah, the homework's going to be hard... anyway, did you hear about the football game?

defs.text: If two people are close, they have a good relationship, like friends, family or lovers.

defs.text: If a game or contest is close, you can't easily see which side is better.
defs.example: The race has been very close up until now.

defs.text: If two things are close, they are similar.

defs.text: Close range/contact/ties etc. is near, not far.
defs.example: They tell us the gun was fired at close range.

defs.text: If you close something, you change it from being open to not open.
defs.example: She watched TV for a while, and then closed her eyes.

defs.text: If something closes, it goes out of business for a short time or permanently.
defs.example: The supermarket closes at 5 o'clock on Saturday.

defs.text: If the distance or time between two different things closes, they get closer together.
defs.example: The government will use the $15 million to close a budget gap.

defs.text: If something closes, it ends.
defs.example: The book closes with the man alone in the house where he started.

defs.text: A party is when people get together for fun or to celebrate something like a birthday.

defs.text: A party is a political group.
defs.example: The Liberal Party will form the government.

defs.text: A party is any group of people who are together for a reason.

defs.text: If you do something for fun, you do it because you enjoy it.

defs.text: Words are the smallest meaningful pieces of a language that can be used on their own.

defs.text: A word is a short conversation.

defs.text: A word is a promise given to someone.

defs.text: A word is a piece of news.

defs.text: The set is the scenery for a theatrical work such as a play, ballet, musical, etc.

defs.text: A set is a group of things that are similar or can be used together.

defs.text: If you set something, you put it into some state or condition.

defs.text: A story is a piece of text that tells someone who reads it about a real or fictional (made up) event.

defs.text: A daughter is a female child of someone.

defs.text: If someone is hurt, they are wounded or in pain.

defs.text: To send something is to make the thing go somewhere without the person. A person sends a letter by putting it in a mailbox. A person can send another person somewhere by telling the person to go there.
defs.example: She needed to send a letter to her mother to say she had arrived safely.

defs.text: News is information about things that happened a short time ago, especially on the radio, TV or in newspapers.
defs.example: Did you hear the news that the war just ended?

defs.text: If something or someone is stupid, it shows a lack of clear thought.
defs.example: I'm so angry. That was a stupid mistake.

defs.text: A piece of furniture to sleep on.
defs.example: At night, I go to bed.

defs.text: The bottom of a river or ocean.
defs.example: The fish was so far down in the water that it was touching the river's bed.

defs.text: a condition of urgency making it necessary to hurry
defs.example: in a hurry to lock the door

defs.text: overly eager speed (and possible carelessness)
defs.example: he soon regretted his haste

defs.text: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
defs.example: in his haste to leave he forgot his book

defs.text: If you hurry, you move or work quickly.
defs.example: After the speech, he had to hurry out the door to the waiting car.

defs.text: A container is full of things if there are many of the things in the container and no more can go in.
defs.example: The cup is full of water. If you try to put more water in, the water will fall onto the table.

defs.text: A full moon is when the moon is a round circle because the sun is shining on the side we can see.
defs.example: I can see the road, because there's a full moon tonight.

defs.text: A person is full when they are satisfied, usually with food.
defs.example: The meal was so large that I was full all day.

defs.text: Something is full when it is total and completed, does not need any additions
A full stop is a punctuation mark "." at the end of a sentence.
defs.example: Don't forget to write full stops at the end of each paragraph!

defs.text: If you save something, you keep it; you do not give it or toss it away.
defs.example: Please save that book for me.

defs.text: If you save someone, you keep them safe or help them survive.
defs.example: You saved my life.

defs.text: If you save information, you put it on a disk or into some kind of long-term memory.
defs.example: He saved the resumé on the floppy disk.

defs.text: If x becomes y, it changes into y or changes to be more y.
defs.example: The boy has become a man.

defs.text: If something becomes someone, it suits them or looks good on them.
defs.example: Nice hat! It really becomes you.

defs.text: Hate is a feeling of strong dislike.
defs.example: My feelings towards him are a mixture of love and hate.

defs.text: A hate is something that you dislike strongly.
defs.example: Did you have any hates or fears when you were there?

defs.text: If you hate something you dislike it strongly.
defs.example: My 3-year old won't eat tomatoes. She just hates them.

defs.text: Food is what people and animals eat for nutrition or pleasure when they are hungry.
defs.example: We grow our own food.

defs.text: Something that is light in color is close to white.
defs.example: The morning sky was very light.

defs.text: Something that is light in weight does not weigh much.
defs.example: I lifted her easily because she was so light.

defs.text: Light may also mean that something is not serious.
defs.example: The light bruise on my leg didn't hurt much.

defs.text: The energy that our eyes sense is light.
defs.example: And dance by the light of the moon.—Buffalo Gals, American folksong

defs.text: If someone talks about a light, he or she means something bright that can be seen.
defs.example: The lights of the city shine all over the valley.

defs.text: If someone lights a fire, the fire starts to burn.
defs.example: Let's light the wood in the fireplace.

defs.text: Something that lights a place makes it less dark.
defs.example: The moon lighted the forest path.

defs.text: A dog is a domestic mammal, related to wolves and foxes, that is often kept as a pet.
defs.example: My pet dog is called "Rover".

defs.text: A land that is controlled by a government.
defs.example: Russia is the largest country in the world.

defs.text: Places outside or far from ; the type of place where farms are. The countryside.
defs.example: We live way out in the country.

defs.text: A certain place, in general.
defs.example: You're in Nascar country now.

defs.text: A kind of (mostly American) music started by people who lived far from cities. Short for country music.
defs.example: I've been listening to a lot of country this month.

defs.text: A clear idea is an idea that is easy to understand.
defs.example: OK, so you need the key. I see. That's clear now.

defs.text: If it is clear that something is a certain way, there can be no mistake about it.
defs.example: The women made it clear that they were doing this only because they wanted to.

defs.text: If you are clear about something, you understand it well.
defs.example: Mike, I want to be clear about what you said, so can you tell me again.

defs.text: If you are clear about something, you make it easy for people to understand you.
defs.example: The coach had been very clear about what he wanted them to do.

defs.text: If you clear something, you move or remove things that you don't want there.
defs.example: You clear the table and I'll get coffee ready.

defs.text: If something clears, it becomes clear.
defs.example: After the fire, it took some time for the air to clear.

defs.text: If something clears, it goes away, leaving the place it was clear.
defs.example: After the fire, it took some time for the smoke to clear.

defs.text: If you clear your throat, you cough lightly to make speaking easier.
defs.example: Tears filled her eyes again, and she cleared her throat. "As soon as I can, I'll get on a plane and meet you."

defs.text: Order is when things are where they should be.
defs.example: I need to take some time to put my things in order.

defs.text: The order of some things means which thing is first, which one is second, which one is last, etc.
defs.example: The children will take turns in order of age.

defs.text: An order is a group of religious people, such as monks or nuns, who follow certain rules.
defs.example: St. Ignatius Loyola founded the Jesuit order in 1537.

defs.text: To order something is to ask someone to sell it to you.
defs.example: At the restaurant, she ordered chicken and potatoes.

defs.text: To order someone to do something is to tell the person that they must do it.
defs.example: The father ordered his children to be quiet.

defs.text: To order things is to put them in a certain order.
defs.example: We need to order them alphabetically.

defs.text: A fact is a piece of information that is true.
defs.example: That is not just my idea, it is a fact.

defs.text: A fact is a piece of information.
defs.example: He collects little-known facts.

defs.text: A captain is a rank in the army between lieutenant and major.
A captain is a rank in the navy between commander and commodore.
A captain is the person who is in charge of a ship or airplane.
defs.example: The captain is the last to abandon ship.

defs.text: A captain is the person who makes all of the decisions on a sports' team.
The number 6.
defs.example: Three and three is six.

defs.text: Something that is hot is high in temperature.
defs.example: The sun is very hot.

defs.text: Someone who is hot is sexually attractive.
defs.example: Woah, that woman is hot!

defs.text: Funny things keep people interested and can make people laugh.

defs.text: Black coffee or tea has no milk in it.
The darkest color; with no light; the color of the sky at night.

defs.text: Blacks are people of a race with dark coloured skin.
defs.example: There were many whites, some blacks and native Americans, and a few Asians.

defs.text: If a company is in the black, it is making a profit. (opposite = in the red)
defs.example: It took a year for the restaurant to get in the black.

defs.text: a form of address for a married woman
If someone or something is alive, it is living or it continues to exist. If you are alive you have life.
defs.example: The doctors tried to keep her alive, but she died an hour after arriving at the hospital.

defs.text: A pick is a choice.
defs.example: His pick for Man of the Year was John Smith.

defs.text: A pick is a tool used to dig.
defs.example: He dug that hole using a pick.

defs.text: A pick is something used to play a guitar with.
defs.example: He forgot his guitar pick.

defs.text: When you pick something, you choose it.
defs.example: I have picked the best people to work on this job.

defs.text: If you pick up something, you lift it.
defs.example: She picked up the glass and put it down again.

defs.text: If you pick up the phone, you answer it.
If you pick something up from somewhere, you go and get it.
defs.example: Mom, can you pick me up from Austin's at 8:00?

defs.text: Your feelings are your emotions, thoughts, and opinions.
defs.example: Many people have strong feelings about the war.

defs.text: A feeling is a signal that your body gives you, such as pain, heat, softness, etc.
defs.example: The feeling of the sun on his face was relaxing.

defs.text: A living thing is a person, animal or plant that is not dead—it is still able to function and grow.
defs.example: Living things grow and make more living things like themselves.

defs.text: A way of earning money.
defs.example: What do you do for a living?

defs.text: a room in a private house or establishment where people can sit and talk and relax
A cause is what leads to something happening.

defs.text: A cause is a goal, aim or principle that people support or fight for.
defs.example: He is fighting for a just cause.

defs.text: To cause something is to make it happen.
defs.example: His careless driving caused the car accident.

defs.text: at or in the front

defs.text: toward the future; forward in time
defs.example: I like to look ahead in imagination to what the future may bring

defs.text: in a forward direction
defs.example: go ahead

defs.example: The boy lost his book some place between home and school.

defs.text: In games, you lose when others do better than you.
defs.example: He lost the card game because he didn't know the rules.

defs.text: A king is the male leader of a country and whose son will probably lead the country.

defs.text: A powerful or influential person.

defs.example: Have you made any plans for tomorrow?

defs.text: A plan is a technical drawing of a room, a building, a city, etc.
defs.example: The plans show this area as housing, with no shopping nearby.

defs.text: If you plan something, you decide what you will do.
defs.example: We need to plan ahead so that we'll be ready.

defs.text: Dinner is the largest meal of the day, usually eaten in the evening.
defs.example: I'm sorry, I'll be late tonight, so I won't be home for dinner.

defs.text: A sort is a kind or type.
defs.example: Red and green are two sorts of apple.

defs.text: To sort is to divide one group of things into smaller groups of things, so that the things in one smaller group are the same as each other in some way.
defs.example: He sorted the apples, putting red apples in one basket and green apples in the other basket.

defs.text: (American football) a play in which a player attempts to carry the ball through or past the opposing team

defs.text: the act of running; traveling on foot at a fast pace

defs.text: the state of being in operation

defs.text: Your boss is the person who tells you what to do at work.
defs.example: My former boss was very happy for the chance to fire me.

defs.text: A boss is a leader in an organisation.
defs.example: The Mayor was an old-style political boss who made his own decisions.

defs.text: When something is alright, that means that it is in good condition.
defs.example: My car is alright.

defs.text: When a person or animal is alright, they are in good health.
defs.example: I had a headache earlier, but now I'm alright.

defs.text: Something that went quite well.
defs.example: The soccer tournament went alright, I guess.

defs.text: When someone is making a promise to a person, he is saying what he plans to do for that person.
defs.example: Jane was angry that John broke his promise to take her out to the movies.

defs.text: When a person promises, he states that he will make certain to do an action.
defs.example: I promise that I will come back home by noon. You can trust me.

defs.text: If something is safe, it is not in danger.
defs.example: I feel safe when I am at home.

defs.text: A book is a lot of paper joined together with writing and pictures printed on them for you to read or write in.

defs.text: A book is a group of stamps, matches, tickets, etc., held together inside a paper cover.

defs.text: If you book something or someone, you reserve them for a certain time.
defs.example: I want to book a hotel room for tomorrow night.

defs.text: If you book someone, you officially put their name in police records for a crime.
defs.example: The police booked him for driving too fast.

defs.text: Something that is colored white
Of a race with light skin or the race that began in Europe, especially northern Europe.
White is one of the colors people can see
The white or clear colored part inside an egg.
A person with fair (light)-colored skin. Usually this means people of the race that began in Europe, especially Northern Europe.
A measure of time, equal to 60 minutes.

defs.text: A small person or thing is not big. It doesn't have much size.
defs.example: A mouse is a small animal. A baby mouse is very small.

defs.text: Something that is perfect has no mistakes, problems, or damage.
defs.example: She answered him in perfect Japanese.

defs.text: Something that is perfect is exactly what was needed or wanted.
defs.example: "Here's the knife." "Oh, yes! Thanks, it's perfect."

defs.example: I believe that in French the passe compose is equivalent to the present perfect tense in English.

defs.text: If you perfect something, you fix all its problems or make it as good as possible.
defs.example: Our leaders have perfected the art of sounding good while saying nothing.

defs.text: If something is special, it is not usual; it is different or important in some way.
defs.example: She is the most special person in my life.

defs.text: particularly interesting; dear; beloved; favored

defs.example: This is a serious problem. We must do something.

defs.text: A person is serious if the person is not laughing or joking, but saying what they mean.
defs.example: I see. When you said the room was empty, you were serious!

defs.text: A company is an organization for doing work for money.
defs.example: He works for a big company.

defs.text: Company is people who are visiting other people; people who are in other peoples' house so that they can talk to the other people, or people who are walking with other people or being somewhere with other people.
defs.example: I can't talk to you on the phone right now, because I have company. (people in the house.)

defs.text: When someone keeps someone else company, they stay with the person.
defs.example: Will you keep me company while I go to mail this letter?

defs.text: A company is a unit of an army, it usually consists of two or three platoons to form a battalion.
To be scared of someone or something means to be afraid of someone or something; to have a fear of someone or something.
defs.example: I'm scared of monsters.

defs.text: Something that is poor is bad quality.
defs.example: The painting was a poor job.

defs.example: Tom is all alone. Poor Tom!

defs.text: The poor are a group of people who have little or no money.
defs.example: This work is to help the poor.

Some soil.

defs.text: Anything made up mostly of rock, sand or soil.
defs.example: Here is some earth.

defs.text: Earth is the third planet from the sun, where we live.
defs.example: The Earth is a planet.

defs.text: A planet, especially one like Earth.
defs.example: He came from a different earth.

defs.text: If something is possible, it is able to be done; doable; not impossible.
defs.example: Life on other planets is possible.

defs.text: If something is possible, it is acceptable.

defs.text: If something is possible, it is likely.
defs.example: Is that possible?

defs.text: When you shoot, you use a weapon to throw something at a very fast speed at someone or something.

defs.text: When you shoot something, you photograph or film something.

defs.text: Touch is ability to feel through the skin by physical contact.
defs.example: After the accident, he lost his sense of touch.

defs.text: A touch of something is a small amount of it.
defs.example: There was a touch of sadness in his voice.

any noise; something that can be heard by the ears.

defs.text: If something sounds a particular way, you think it is that way when you hear or read about it.
defs.example: The restaurant sounds great.

defs.text: situated at the top or highest position

defs.text: The highest part of something; the upper part; the part people can put things on.

The winning of a individual or a team.

defs.text: To achieve victory.

defs.text: If you are glad about something, you are happy about it.

defs.text: If you are glad to do something, you will do it happily.
defs.example: "Can you get this door for me?" "Sure, I'd be glad to."

defs.text: If you have control over someone or something, you can make it do what you want.
defs.example: He should try to take control and tell the other handlers what to do.

defs.example: If you turn off your TV with the remote control, it continues to use a quarter of normal power.

defs.text: If you control something, you make it do what you want.
defs.example: Too many people are overweight because they can't control their eating behaviour.

defs.text: If you control something, you do not let its numbers or size grow too much.
defs.example: The new plan should control inflation.

defs.text: Human rights, life, nature, etc. belong or relate to people, not machines or animals.
defs.example: Every person has human rights.

defs.text: A human is a person; a member of the Homo sapiens species.

defs.text: A road in a city with buildings on the sides and places where people can walk.

defs.text: Dance is body movement done to music.

defs.text: A degree awarded by a university.

defs.text: If you dream about something, you wish for it.

defs.text: If you write a book, an article, a computer program, a piece of music, etc., you create it.

defs.text: A sweet person or thing pleases or is nice.

If you are lucky, you have a lot of luck.

defs.text: Coffee is a dark brown drink that is very popular around the world.

defs.text: Something's return is when it is given back.

defs.example: This store does not allow returns unless the customer has a receipt.

defs.text: The return of something to a particular state is the change back to that state.
When you return something, you give/put it back.
defs.example: He returned the lawnmower back to John.

defs.text: When you return to something or somewhere, you go/come back to it.
defs.example: He returned to China after his trip to Germany.

defs.text: If a feeling, problem, thought, etc. returns, it comes back.
defs.example: I thought I was better, but the pain in my back has returned.

defs.text: If you return to an activity, you start it again.

defs.text: A date is a particular day in a month or year.
defs.example: "What's the date on Friday?" "Uh, the 17th, I think."

defs.text: A date is an agreement to meet on particular day at a particular time.
defs.example: Can we set a date for the next meeting? How about June 21st?

defs.text: A date is a time when you go out with a romantic partner.
defs.example: I've got a date with Michael tonight. We're going to that new restaurant.

defs.text: You date is the person you are meeting romantically.
defs.example: Who's your date for the dance?

defs.text: If you date something, you write the date on it.
defs.example: You need to date this form at the top, here.

defs.text: If you date something, you find out how old it is, especially something very old.
defs.example: We have not been successful in dating the painting, though we believe it is from the 17th century.

defs.text: If something dates, it goes out of style and looks old fashioned.
defs.example: Unfortunately, this jacket has dated rather more quickly than I had hoped.

defs.text: If something dates from a particular time, it first existed at that time.
defs.example: The earliest electronic computers date from the mid-20th century (around 1940–1945).

defs.text: Fall is the name for autumn used only in North America, named after the falling of leaves during the season. It is the season when the weather is getting colder, after summer and before winter.
defs.example: These plants are growing big and they will be ready to eat in the fall.

defs.text: A fall or falls or waterfall is a part of a river where water is falling.
defs.example: We went to the falls to eat lunch outside and watch the water falling.

defs.text: A fall is when people suffered a loss of greatness or status, such as the fall of Rome.
When something or someone falls, it moves down quickly down through the air because nothing is holding it. It moves to a lower position because of gravity.
defs.example: The apple fell from the tree.

defs.text: When someone falls, they can mean coming down to the ground on purpose, lying with the face down.
defs.example: He fell to the floor and begged for mercy.

defs.text: Falling is when someone or something has been defeated.
defs.example: The Romans fell to the Goths in 410 AD.

defs.text: If someone is given to doing something, they do it regularly.
defs.example: My father's given to making long speeches about when he was a boy.

defs.text: If someone is given to something, they wear, use, or do it often.
defs.example: When she got older, she was given to elegant clothes and long speeches.

defs.text: If something is your fault, you did something wrong or didn't do something right.
defs.example: It doesn't matter whose fault it is, let's work together to make it right.

defs.text: A fault is a problem or a mistake.
defs.example: We found a few faults in the plan, but we'll fix them later.

defs.text: A fault in your character is something about you that is not nice or good.
defs.example: The other girls thought that her only fault was that she was really stupid.

defs.text: A fault is a long crack in the earth.
defs.example: The earthquake occurred near the San Andreas fault.

defs.text: If something is straight, it does not bend, or turn. It continues in one direction.

defs.text: Someone who is straight is heterosexual; being attracted to those of the opposite sex.
If something goes straight, it continues to move in one direction without turning.

defs.text: A song is some music with words in verse.
defs.example: That song sounds beautiful.

defs.text: The future is the time of something that hasn't happen yet. The study of the future is known as futurology.
defs.example: I will be more careful in the future.

defs.text: A look forward.

defs.text: A future event is one that hasn't happened yet but will happen.

defs.text: The path which one takes to reach a certain place.

defs.text: If a person, place or situation is calm, it is peaceful and quiet.
defs.example: There's no wind and the lake is calm.

defs.text: Something wonderful is exciting, excellent, and creates feelings of wonder.

defs.text: If someone is mad, they are angry.

defs.text: If someone is mad, they are insane.

defs.text: To be mad about someone or something means to like someone or something very much.
A drop is a very small amount of a liquid.

defs.text: A drop is the fall of something.
defs.example: There was a drop in the prices last week.

defs.text: To fall, or to let something fall.

defs.text: When you learn something, you start to know how to do things that you didn't know before.

defs.text: When you learn something, you start to know something that you didn't know before.
defs.example: I've just learned that I've been adopted.

defs.text: When you learn, you start to know more than you knew before.
defs.example: You have to learn from your own mistakes.

defs.text: A step is a movement of the foot
defs.example: Take one step forward to win the game.

defs.text: A step is one of several actions or processes taken to achieve a goal.
defs.example: Heating the oven is one step needed to bake bread.

defs.text: A step is a surface used to walk upwards. Most often there are several steps, one above the other.
defs.example: One must walk up the steps to get to the top of the building.

defs.text: When you step, you move one foot.
defs.example: When you walk, you step many times.

defs.text: If something is absolutely true, correct, etc., it's 100% so.
defs.example: I agree. You're absolutely right.

defs.text: If something is absolutely beautiful, brilliant, etc., it's very much so.
defs.example: "It was wonderful," Martha said. "Absolutely wonderful! The best!"

defs.text: You say there is absolutely nothing, to emphasise that there is nothing.
defs.example: I have absolutely no idea why he said that.

defs.text: If something is early, it is sooner than expected.

defs.text: If something is clean, it is free from dirt

defs.text: If a technology is clean, it doesn't produce much pollution.

defs.text: A clean piece of paper, start, etc. has nothing from before: no writing, no history, etc.
defs.example: Why don't you get a clean piece of paper and start over.

defs.text: A piece is a part of something that can be or has been separated from it.

defs.text: A piece is one example of a class or set of things.
defs.example: He put a piece of wood on the fire.

defs.text: A piece is something that is made by an artist.

defs.example: He jumped off the wall and landed on his feet.

defs.text: When an airplane lands, it comes down from the air onto the ground.

defs.text: When you land an airplane, you use the controls to bring it down on the ground.

defs.text: A wonder is something that makes a person think.

defs.text: If you wonder about something, you think about it because you want to know more about it.
defs.example: I wonder when they will be home.

defs.example: I wonder if you could give me a hand with the door.

defs.text: To state something is to say it as a fact.

defs.example: People laughed at the boy because he was weird.

defs.text: Laws are the official rules of a government or organisation.

defs.text: The law is the police.

Law is the study of laws.

defs.example: I'm worried about not having enough money.

defs.text: A report is a description of something that has happened.

defs.text: A report is a document that gives the results of a study of a particular situation.

defs.example: He could hear the report of the explosion.

defs.text: If the news reports something, it tells us about it.
defs.example: The journalist reported that there were riots in the city.

defs.text: When you report something that has happened, you describe it.
defs.example: They reported to the police that their car had been stolen.

defs.text: If you report somebody for something they've done wrong, you tell an official about the problem.
defs.example: The restaurant was reported to the city because of the dangerous kitchen.

defs.example: Visitors to the school should report to the office.

defs.text: A pass is a piece of paper, plastic, etc. that allows somebody to enter a building, vehicle, or area.

defs.text: If you pass a test, exam, etc., you get a score that is good enough, often over 50%.
defs.example: You passed the test. In fact, you got 7 out of 10 correct.

defs.text: An officer is someone who holds office (meaning, has authority).
defs.example: The judge is an important officer of the court.

defs.text: A police officer is an official person who stops criminals and helps people.

defs.text: A girlfriend is a girl or young woman who is in a romantic relationship with another person.
defs.example: Jeremy had been having trouble with his girlfriend.

defs.text: A girlfriend can be any friend who is female.
The sound of someone laughing, or the action of laughing.
defs.example: We had lots of good laughs at the party.

defs.text: Someone laughs when they make a sound with their mouth because they think something is funny. It can sound like "ha ha", "ho ho", "hee hee", etc.
defs.example: That was a really good joke. I've never laughed so hard!

defs.text: The way a thing smells; the substance in the air that people can smell.
defs.example: The smell of the flowers is very good.

defs.text: If you smell something, you use the nose to sense it.
defs.example: She put her nose near the flowers and breathed in to smell them.

defs.text: If something smells, it gently put a substance that people can smell into the air.
defs.example: The flowers smell very good.

defs.text: Something that is broken is not as it should be because it has been damaged or injured
defs.example: The broken cup lay in pieces on the floor.

defs.text: If something in a game, such as a gun, is broken, it is overpowered
A short word for mother.
A mum is kind of flower.
If you are honest, you do not hide the truth; you don't lie, cheat, or steal.
defs.example: My parents were quite honest with me about things to do with sex.

defs.text: The third thing is the one that is number three (3) in order.
defs.example: I have two older brothers. I'm the third child.

defs.text: The form of a verb that is used when the subject of a sentence is not the one making the statement. Some pronouns that are used with the third person are he, she, it, one, they, and who.
defs.example: "Is" is the third person singular of "be".

defs.text: A form of storytelling that uses verbs in the third person to show that the storyteller is not a character in the story.
The act of visiting.
defs.example: I paid a visit to my grandmother last weekend to see how she was doing.

defs.text: When you visit someone, you meet the person.
defs.example: I visit my friend Bethsy at her house every Tuesday.

defs.text: When you visit a place, you see the place.
defs.example: When I went to Paris, I visited the Eiffel Tower.

defs.text: Your mama is your mother.
defs.example: Mama, what's for dinner?

defs.text: A judge is a person who decides or chooses.
defs.example: The judge decides cases.

defs.text: A judge is a leader.
defs.example: Samson was a judge of Israel.

defs.text: To choose, decide.
defs.example: He judged in favor of the defendant.

defs.text: To evaluate (decide if something is good or bad).
defs.example: They judged the beauty pageant.

defs.text: To estimate.
defs.example: I would judge that the lake holds a million gallons.

defs.text: A piece of glass in a wall to let people see through it.
defs.example: He looked out the window.

defs.text: If you feel hungry, you want to eat something and your stomach feels empty.
defs.example: There are too many poor children who are always hungry.

defs.text: When there is a relationship between things, there is a connection.
defs.example: There is a clear relationship between fire and heat.

defs.text: When people are connected by family, there is a relationship between them.
defs.example: There is a family relationship between Bob Smith and John Smith.

defs.text: When people are friends or partners, they have a relationship.
defs.example: John is the boyfriend of Joan. They have a relationship.

defs.text: When you prove something, you demonstrate that it is for real and true.
defs.example: I will prove my method is more effective than yours.

defs.text: Private is for only one person or a small number of people to see or know.
defs.example: I don't want to tell you how much money I have; that's private.

defs.text: One side of a house; a high, flat part of a building.
defs.example: All four walls of the room are painted in blue.

defs.text: A solid barrier between two areas.
defs.example: There is a wall between the two gardens.

defs.text: A seat is something to sit on.
defs.example: Pull up a seat and sit down.

defs.text: The seat is a part of the clothes covering the buttocks.
defs.example: The seat of your pants is muddy.

defs.text: Seat is where something is, at the centre of things.
defs.example: The town was the county seat, where the county council met.

defs.text: The position of something is the place where the thing is.
defs.example: The position of the table is two metres from the wall.

defs.text: A post of employment; a job.
If you realize something, you become aware of it.
defs.example: John just realized that he had left his umbrella at home.

defs.text: If something is realized, it is made real.
defs.example: My dreams of starting my own company have been realized.

defs.text: A machine is a man-made object with moving parts.
defs.example: I'm putting the clothes in the washing machine. Is there anything you want washed?

defs.text: the act of traveling by foot
defs.example: walking is a healthy form of exercise

defs.text: An art is a skill that produces works of creative expression and can be mastered through study and practice. Arts are often contrasted with sciences.
defs.example: ing, music and writing are arts.

defs.text: Art is creation by means of an art. examples of art are paintings and photographs, but songs and even buildings can be art, too.
defs.example: The gallery has many pieces of art.
